newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Aristocrat says to seek Nevada licence.
newsitem.headline: Aristocrat says to seek Nevada licence.

text.p: Aristocrat Leisure Ltd said on Monday it still intends to apply for a gaming licence in the U.S. state of Nevada, but would wait for the result of its appeal against allegations by gaming regulators in Colorado.

"We have not yet applied for a licence in Nevada. We will wait for the outcome of our appeal in Colorado, but we intend to apply by December, 1997," Aristocrat executive chairman John Dougall told reporters after the release of its annual results.

Last month, the Colorado Limited Gaming Commission refused to renew Aristocrat's licence to operate in the U.S. state and alleged the company was under the influence and control of parties considered unsuitable.

Aristocrat plans to appeal against the Colorado ruling, which would start on October 27. The Cherokee Tribal Gaming Commission in North Carolina had recently suspended Aristocrat's vendor licence pending the outcome of the Colorado hearing.
Earlier Aristocrat said its net profit rose to A$23.32 million from A$17.84 million the previous year and was above the A$22.3 million forecast in the prospectus.

Dougall said the group was still assessing the impact of the previous Islamist-led Turkish government decision last December to close casinos, because of concerns about their demoralising effect on Turkish society.
"We had not forecast any substantial business in 1998 out of Turkey. The guys in our European operating are looking at that," Dougall said.

At 12.30 p.m. (0230 GMT), Aristocrat shares were unchanged at A$2.70, despite a near two percent fall in the broader market. The result was slightly ahead of market median estimates. -- Kevin Morrison 61-2 9373-1813
